dashboard.label: Set up RHEL Audit Verification
dashboard.description: Connect supported, already-indexed logs. No endpoint or collection settings are changed.

div.h1: Your logs. A clear starting point.
div.p: Find the records you already collect, confirm your expected systems, and check the connection to your dashboard.

div.div: Setup readiness is not control acceptance. Discovery cannot establish your host inventory, prove lossless delivery, or identify the person who physically handled a USB.

section.p: Already forwarding logs? Choose their indexes. Not sure? Select up to five likely indexes and run discovery. No search runs until you click.
section.label: Accessible indexes
section.p: Last 24 hours · up to 10,001 sampled records · 25-second search limit. Samples are suggestions, not a complete inventory.
section.label: Or enter exact index names, separated by commas

section.h2: 2. Confirm your expected systems and feeds
section.p: Check discovered feeds, then add them below. Existing inventory is loaded when possible. Import CSV to include systems that are not sending logs; discovery cannot find silent systems.
The suggested 3,600 seconds is not a policy requirement. Confirm an appropriate threshold for each feed.
section.label: Import expected-feed CSV (replaces the draft, not the saved inventory)
Expected-feed CSV · editable preview · maximum 200 rows
I confirm the enabled feeds belong to the Red Hat systems I intend to audit. Discovery alone does not establish that.

section.p: Only app search scope, expected-feed inventory, and the setup-complete flag change. Original logs, forwarders, audit rules, roles, and retention stay untouched. The legacy overview remains separately configured.
section.label: Apply this exact preview. I have reviewed the inventory and will not run setup from another window at the same time.
section.p: Administrator write permission is required. A server-side backup is saved first; the prior inventory is never overwritten.

details.p: Enter the backup ID shown after save. Restore refuses settings changed since that save. Backups live in this app's aulx_setup configuration; retain them during upgrades.
details.label: Backup ID
Restore the previous app settings identified by this backup.

section.p: Checks the saved feed selection under your current account. It does not generate test events or mark controls accepted.

If a feed is missing, confirm its index, host identity, time, access rights and source collection. A zero count is not proof that logging is disabled. USB session context is not physical-user attribution.

div.p: Standalone Splunk Enterprise first. Clustered/Cloud deployments and inventories above 200 feeds should use the managed installation guide. No automatic compliance acceptance or source changes.
